overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the July 6, 2012 IT planning group was not a public body and no quorum of the Committee met. It also flagged, without ruling, a possible location problem at the June 19 open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a de facto 'IT MOU Dissolution Subcommittee' met on July 6, 2012 without a posted open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the group that met was not a public body in its own right, and neither meeting involved a quorum of the Committee, there was no improper deliberation under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised by complainant: the AG noted that the June 19, 2012 open session may have been held in a location not truly open to the public.
allegations.key_passage: Although not raised by the complainant, we note that an open meeting held in a location that is not truly open to the public does not comply with the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
